why: Lead-vehicle emergency braking is a plausible but intentionally stress-biased event. The ranges cover moderate-to-hard braking for 1-4 s and activation at an 8-35 m following gap; the simulator additionally rejects deceleration above mu*g. FHWA reports over 36,000 crash, near-crash, and baseline events across over 5.4 million SHRP2 trips (about 0.0067 event/trip); exposure is conservatively rounded up to 0.01/trip. This is a broad safety-event proxy, not a measured lead-braking rate, and must be replaced by fleet-specific brake-event logs before deployment. Source: https://highways.dot.gov/safety/learn-safety/road-safety-fundamentals-html-version/unit-3-measuring-safety
